The nugget of an estimated autocorrelation range

Source: R/cross-validation.R
sac_nugget.Rd

The nugget variance of the variogram model behind a estimate_sac_range() result: the model's semivariance as the separation shrinks to zero, i.e. measurement error plus variation at scales shorter than the first lag of the empirical variogram. It is extrapolated to zero from that lag, not observed, so it is only as good as the first lag is short: attr(x, "first_lag") says where the extrapolation starts. With lags = "adaptive" (the default) that is the separation of the closest pairs of points; with lags = "equal" it is the middle of a bin cutoff * max_dist / n_lags wide, which on a dense layer can be many times the spacing of close pairs, and structure shorter than that bin is then counted as nugget.

Usage

sac_nugget(x)

Arguments

x

A sac_range object, or anything else.

Value

A single number: the nugget in the units of the response's variance; NA_real_ when x carries no fitted model (a bare NA from a run that could not fit anything, a rejected result with too few lag bins to fit, or an object that is not a sac_range).

Details

Three more attributes say how far to trust it. attr(x, "nugget_at_bound") is TRUE when the fit put the nugget at its lower bound (0, or within 1e-4 of the sill): that is the bound and not an estimate, and a criterion that uses it as a noise variance has no penalty left. attr(x, "short_lag_semivariance") is the semivariance of nearest-neighbour pairs, computed with no model: each location is paired with the nearest other location (short_lag_pairs and short_lag_dist give the number of such pairs and their median separation). A semivariance does not fall as the lag shrinks, so this value bounds the nugget from above, up to its sampling error; a fitted nugget well above it is contradicted by the closest pairs. attr(x, "zero_lag_semivariance") exists where locations were visited more than once (zero_lag_pairs is not 0): it is the semivariance of every pair of rows that share a location, that is, the variance between visits to one place. That is the measurement part of the nugget, observed and not extrapolated, without the variation at scales below the spacing of the locations, so it bounds the nugget from below. Such pairs are at no lag and are in no bin of the variogram: the model, and so the nugget, describe positive separations. The variogram fit uses the bound, though: where it rests on 30 degrees of freedom or more (rows less locations) the nugget is not let under it, and attr(x, "nugget_floor") holds the value (0 when there is no floor). With detrend = "reml" the model is built from the REML parameters and takes no floor: its nugget can come out below the variance between visits, and nugget_floor is 0. A nugget equal to its floor is the variance between visits, a measurement, and nugget_at_bound stays FALSE for it.

When attr(x, "lag_fallback") is TRUE the result is the equal-lag one although adaptive lags were asked for (see "The lags" in estimate_sac_range), and its nugget is extrapolated from the first equal bin.

The nugget is carried as the nugget attribute of every classed result, identified or rejected, because it is the number a resolution criterion for a tessellation needs (the short-lag variance that no cell can average away). On a result refused for want of spatial structure it is the variance of the modelled variable, which is the nugget of the model that refusal supports.

See also

estimate_sac_range, which produces the object.

Other cross-validation: area_of_applicability(), cv_bayes(), cv_block_size_sweep(), cv_gwr(), cv_rf(), cv_spatial(), estimate_sac_range(), fold_separation(), gwr_model_selection(), make_folds(), select_features_forward()

Examples

if (requireNamespace("gstat", quietly = TRUE)) {
  library(sf)
  # A field with a real nugget: half a unit of white noise on a unit sill.
  set.seed(3)
  n <- 250
  xy <- data.frame(x = 5e5 + runif(n, 0, 1000), y = 5e6 + runif(n, 0, 1000))
  D  <- as.matrix(dist(xy))
  xy$z <- as.numeric(t(chol(exp(-D / 150) + diag(0.5, n))) %*% rnorm(n))
  r <- estimate_sac_range(st_as_sf(xy, coords = c("x", "y"), crs = 32632), "z")
  print(sac_nugget(r))  # the fitted nugget variance, on the sill's scale
  attr(r, "nugget_at_bound")         # FALSE: an estimate, not the bound
  attr(r, "short_lag_semivariance")  # what the closest pairs say, no model
  attr(r, "zero_lag_pairs")          # 0: no location was visited twice
  sac_nugget(NA)        # nothing fitted: NA
}
#> [1] 0.4253438
#> [1] NA
